title: Boot refused: new required field has no literal default to backfill
body: A model added a `required` field to a concept whose table already has rows, but the field declares no literal `default` -- so SchemaLifecycleExecutor has no value to backfill existing rows with (LNCH-1 Phase 5) and refuses the boot rather than leaving NOT NULL half-enforced. Two distinct causes produce this same refusal: (1) no default at all -- add a literal `default` to the field (e.g. `"default": "pending"`); a `defaultExpression`-only field is NOT backfilled automatically in v1 (expression backfills are unsupported), so replace it with a literal default or make the field optional. (2) the new required field is a bond/FK reference -- a bond has no automatic backfill possible (its value would need to reference an existing row's real key); make the field optional, or use the itemized destructive-acknowledgment path (`Build-NpdevApp.ps1 -Upgrade -AcknowledgeDestructive`) to recreate the table instead. The refusal message names every offending `table.column`; the stored fingerprint stays stale so a fixed retry converges cleanly. See docs/SCHEMA_EVOLUTION.md#new-required-fields.
signature: schema change adds new required field(s) to table(s) with existing data, but no literal default is available to backfill automatically (lnch-1 phase 5): [users.phone (no default declared -- declare a literal default or make it optional)]. declare a literal <id> on the field, or make it optional -- see docs/schema_evolution.md#new-required-fields
fix: Add a literal `default` to the field (not a defaultExpression, which is not auto-backfilled in v1), or make it optional. If the field is a required bond/FK, make it optional or use the acknowledged destructive path instead -- there is no automatic backfill for a bond's value.
